newsitem.title: UK: GOLF-WORLD'S BEST FORCED TO TAKE BACK SEAT.
newsitem.headline: GOLF-WORLD'S BEST FORCED TO TAKE BACK SEAT.

text.p: The forecast before the start of the British Open was that it would be a fight between the world's top players, most of whom were in great form.
At the halfway stage, not one of the world's top 10 figure on the leader board.
The highest placed of that exalted group is Australian Greg Norman, and he is joint 13th, nine strokes behind Britain's Darren Clarke who heads the field on 133.
World number one Tiger Woods is joint 53rd on four-over-par 146 and South African Ernie Els, ranked second, joint 28th on 144. Local favourite Colin Montgomerie, ranked fourth, is joint 43rd on 145.

The fearsome links course of Royal Troon has been a great leveller and no respecter of reputations on the opening two days despite showing its more benign face on Friday when the wind dropped and the sun shone.
The forecast for Saturday and Sunday is more calm, sunny weather which will make it harder for the top ranked players to overhaul the current squad of leaders.
Their hope is that their experience will see them through in tough conditions and provide a spate of high scores among the rest. All this week they have been saying they hope the wind really blows.
Woods was only two strokes off missing the cut, something that has not happened to him since he turned professional nearly a year ago.
But he still insists he is playing well. "I'm hitting the ball very well this week. Unfortunately I just happened to have two bad holes," he said.
Those bad holes were a triple bogey in the first round and a disastrous quadruple bogey on Friday.
"If you take away those bad holes, I'm three-under. So I'm not playing that bad," he said.
Clarke, two strokes ahead of the field, is beginning to feel he can pull off a surprise win over the world's best.
"If I can get myself into contention on Sunday afternoon, I do believe I can give it a go," he said.
